Title: Admin Auth Hardening Current State
Content:
Admin, user-management, settings, audit, diagnostics, and restore policies require an authenticated user with an explicit Admin role claim. AnonymousAccess=Admin, AuthenticatedDefaultRole=Admin, AutoEditorForAuthenticatedUsers, X-Api-Key compatibility, Auth:Enabled=false, and OpenLocalEditorCompatibility do not satisfy privileged policies. Anonymous access is clamped to Viewer-only behavior; authenticated default role is clamped to Viewer or Editor. First-admin setup remains anonymous but loopback/token constrained. The /admin Configuration tab exposes allowlisted MemorySmithOptions settings through AdminSettingsService, includes per-setting info-circle help text, handles sensitive values as write-only, persists edits to appsettings.LocalDevelopment.json or MemorySmith:SettingsOverridePath, reloads configuration, and records settings.updated audit entries.

Auth self-lockout guardrail (TSK-0300): AdminSettingsService.TryValidateCrossSettingConstraints now verifies that at least one sign-in method (LocalPasswordEnabled or any external provider) would remain active before allowing a settings save. The AdminController.SetProviderEnabled endpoint also checks that disabling a provider does not leave zero active sign-in methods. Both paths return a clear error message instead of allowing total lockout.
